protocol.name: mudhuts_power_button
protocol.copyright: This protocol is part of mudhuts, a from-scratch Wayland compositor. It is not shared with or endorsed by any other project.

interface.name: mudhuts_power_button_manager_v1

description.summary: get notified of hardware power-button presses

interface.description:
mudhuts never acts on the power button itself while any client holds a mudhuts_power_button_v1 object — deciding what a press (or a held press, or a double press, ...) should do is entirely up to whichever layer-shell client(s) bind this. mudhuts only falls back to its own default action (ending the current session, i.e. a logout — never an immediate poweroff) when *no* client holds one, so a system unaware of the power button at all still fails safe instead of shutting the machine down on a single stray press.
A hardware power button is also wired into systemd-logind directly (independent of any Wayland client); mudhuts takes logind's handle-power-key inhibitor lock for as long as it's running a real TTY session specifically so logind's own default (an immediate poweroff) never races this protocol's own handling.

request.name: get_power_button
request.description: Any client may make this request; there is no ownership limit; every currently-bound mudhuts_power_button_v1 gets every button event.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Does not affect any mudhuts_power_button_v1 objects already created from it.

interface.name: mudhuts_power_button_v1

description.summary: one client's subscription to power-button events

interface.description: While this object exists, mudhuts sends it every press and release of the hardware power button and takes no default action of its own on either — entirely this client's call, including whether to act on a bare press at all or wait for some pattern (a hold, a double press, ...) before doing anything.

event.name: button

description.summary: the power button was pressed or released

event.description: serial is a new serial for this event specifically (usable with requests elsewhere that take a serial, e.g. to grant a session lock, drive a confirmation surface's popup grab, ...); time is the original input event's own millisecond timestamp.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Once every client's mudhuts_power_button_v1 has been destroyed, mudhuts resumes handling the power button itself (see mudhuts_power_button_manager_v1's own description) starting with the next press — a press already in progress (pressed sent, no matching released yet) when the last one is destroyed is not retroactively handled.
